map.reading: The three existing segments survive a refresh and keep their exact names: none of their definitions changed, and each gained some external support. The pre-launch maker is the best-evidenced — public builder-forum threads discuss this exact job, name an annual price, and explicitly value not paying monthly. The multi-site studio gained the strongest market evidence: a visible layer of fixed-price marketplace gigs that build one-page sites for other people's clients, including domain connection and forms. The illustrator remains the most inferred of the three; the best support is indirect, namely reviews naming free-tier branding and the vendor subdomain as what professionals outgrow. Four candidates are new. Two come from observed usage rather than stated pain: commission artists publishing itemised price-and-terms sheets for high-ticket work, and volunteer-run dated fan events publishing programme, guest and application pages. Both are plainly real workflows on this product today, and for both the purchase motive is unproven — nearly every observed page sits on a free vendor subdomain, which in those communities may read as normal rather than cheap. One is a channel: template designers, where the maker programme's own documentation ties a paid plan to a 70 percent revenue share, and an independent Etsy and Gumroad market for these templates confirms buyer demand exists. One is adjacent: marketplace sellers told by their own seller-education literature to build a signup page on an owned domain reached by a QR code on packaging — a requirement that happens to match three separate capabilities, with the same sources recommending free alternatives in the next breath. Counterevidence worth carrying forward. First, structural: migration and alternatives guides are explicit that a one-page product is one URL with anchors, with no second page, no blog and no per-post URLs, and they frame outgrowing it as the normal trajectory for anything commercial. That is the blocking objection for the studio and small-business segments and nothing in the supplied catalogue answers it. Second, paywall shape: independent reviews state that forms and widgets begin at the Pro Standard tier, so the free tier cannot take a contact enquiry — precisely the moment several of these buyers discover the gate. Third, two segments I declined to promote: musicians, because the category is crowded with purpose-built pre-save and smart-link tools offering custom domains at comparable prices; and single-property real estate, where cheaper per-listing specialists with lead capture already exist. Fourth, the large activism and mutual-aid usage of this product is usage without visible purchase: those pages are overwhelmingly free-tier and the operators have no revenue, so I treated them as counterevidence to a heavy-usage-implies-buyers reading rather than as a segment. Every why_them here is a hypothesis. No first-party customer evidence for this product was found at all — consistent with the brief's note that no testimonial exists on its own site — so no outcome claim in this map is supportable yet.
map.note: Coverage gaps. Reddit is not fetchable by this agent, and it is the single most likely venue for this product's buyer complaints; every attempt to reach buyer voices there failed, so the map leans on forum posts, marketplace listings and live published pages instead. That biases the evidence toward observable artefacts over stated pain. Search results also arrived as summaries rather than raw quotations in several cases, so the returned URLs should be fetched and read before any claim here is treated as sourced. Unsuccessful or thin searches: direct buyer complaints about hitting plan ceilings; anything on uptime, ownership, company size or longevity, which is the blocking objection for the client-site studio and is unanswered in both the supplied catalogue and the public sources I reached; consent and data-processing terms for forms, which matters for the discount-for-email segment; and any first-party customer story, testimonial or named case study for this product. Leads seen but not promoted for want of evidence: cafes, food trucks and small restaurants using a one-pager as a QR-code menu, where a template and widget ecosystem clearly exists but I found no operator voice and no purchase evidence, so it needs its own pass; coaches and course creators running a payment-enabled sales page, where free payment links undercut the need; and local service solos such as tattoo artists, where booking-specific platforms own the workflow end to end. Population figures are unknown throughout and I have not estimated any. Segment kinds are descriptive labels, not a quota; four of the seven are core-shaped buyers and I did not manufacture an influencer or unintended-use segment to fill the taxonomy. One capability caveat: the maker programme underpinning the template-designer candidate is not present in the supplied capability catalogue, so that candidate's required capabilities list only the supplied template-building, template-sharing and premium-template facts.

Form-category templates collect emails and feedback, with selling gated to Pro Plus or higher; the condition must travel with any payment-related use.
